Payment blocks occur for several reasons: Invoice Verification block (R) - set automatically when 3-way matching fails (quantity or price variance beyond tolerance during MIRO); Manual block - set by finance/AP team (FB02 or MRBR); Vendor master block - vendor account itself is blocked (FK05). "[{""from"":""system"",""value"":""You are an expert ERP consultant with deep knowledge of SAP and Microsoft Dynamics AX (D365 F&O). Standard Price (S): a fixed price set for the material that does not change with actual purchasing prices. All GR postings are made at this standard price. Price differences between actual PO price and standard price are posted to a Price Difference account. Used for: finished goods (FERT) and semi-finished goods (HALB) where production costs are planned. Advantages: stable inventory values, variance analysis highlighting inefficiencies. Moving Average Price (V): automatically recalculates after each goods receipt to reflect the actual average purchase price. Formula: (Current Stock Value + New GR Value) / (Current Stock Qty + New GR Qty). Used for: raw materials (ROH) and trading goods (HAWA) where market prices fluctuate. Advantages: realistic inventory valuation reflecting actual costs. In AX/D365, equivalent valuation methods are configured in Item Model Groups (InventModelGroup): Standard Cost = SAP Standard Price, Weighted Average = closest to SAP Moving Average.""}]"

In inter-plant stock transfers (within one company code): stock transfer order (STO) with movement type 641 (GI from sending plant), stock appears as 'Stock in Transfer' in MARD table (field UMLME) until goods receipt at receiving plant (movement type 101). In intercompany scenarios: billing document issued by selling company, goods in transit period before GR at buying company. Accounting treatment during transit: Goods in Transit account debited (asset account showing stock owned but not yet at destination). In AX/D365, goods in transit is managed through Transfer Orders (InventTransferTable) where ship status creates 'Shipped' inventory status visible in InventTrans with StatusIssue=Deducted at source and StatusReceipt=Purchased at destination before receipt posting.""}]"

Step 1: Purchase Requisition (PR) - an internal document requesting procurement (ME51N). Step 2: Request for Quotation (RFQ) - sent to potential vendors for pricing (ME41). Step 3: Quotation Comparison - comparing vendor quotes (ME49). Step 4: Purchase Order (PO) - formal order to selected vendor (ME21N, tables EKKO/EKPO). Step 5: Goods Receipt (GR) - recording receipt of materials (MIGO, movement type 101, tables MKPF/MSEG). Step 6: Invoice Verification (IV) - matching vendor invoice to PO and GR (MIRO, tables RBKP/RSEG). Step 7: Payment Run - automatic payment to vendor (F110). Integration points: PR → PO (reference), GR → PO history updated, IV → 3-way match (PO+GR+Invoice), Payment → FI clears vendor open item.""}]"

Step 1: Purchase Requisition (PR) - an internal document requesting procurement (ME51N). Step 2: Request for Quotation (RFQ) - sent to potential vendors for pricing (ME41). Step 3: Quotation Comparison - comparing vendor quotes (ME49). Step 4: Purchase Order (PO) - formal order to selected vendor (ME21N, tables EKKO/EKPO). Step 5: Goods Receipt (GR) - recording receipt of materials (MIGO, movement type 101, tables MKPF/MSEG). Step 6: Invoice Verification (IV) - matching vendor invoice to PO and GR (MIRO, tables RBKP/RSEG). Step 7: Payment Run - automatic payment to vendor (F110). Integration points: PR → PO (reference), GR → PO history updated, IV → 3-way match (PO+GR+Invoice), Payment → FI clears vendor open item.""}]"

The three documents that must match: 1) Purchase Order (EKKO/EKPO) - agreed quantity and price, 2) Goods Receipt (MKPF/MSEG) - actual quantity received, 3) Vendor Invoice (RBKP/RSEG) - vendor's billed quantity and price. During Invoice Verification (MIRO), SAP automatically compares: Invoice quantity vs GR quantity (quantity check), Invoice price vs PO price (price check). Tolerances are configured per company code. If invoice exceeds tolerance, it is automatically blocked (payment block R). Finance can review blocked invoices in MRBR. This ensures you only pay for what was ordered AND received at the agreed price.""}]"

In AX/D365: Free Text Credit Notes for customers (CustFreeInvoice with negative amounts), Vendor Credit Notes (VendInvoiceJour with Credit Note type). The principle is identical - credit reduces balance, debit increases it.""}]"

Standard Price (S): a fixed price set for the material that does not change with actual purchasing prices. All GR postings are made at this standard price. Price differences between actual PO price and standard price are posted to a Price Difference account. Used for: finished goods (FERT) and semi-finished goods (HALB) where production costs are planned. Advantages: stable inventory values, variance analysis highlighting inefficiencies. Moving Average Price (V): automatically recalculates after each goods receipt to reflect the actual average purchase price. Formula: (Current Stock Value + New GR Value) / (Current Stock Qty + New GR Qty). Used for: raw materials (ROH) and trading goods (HAWA) where market prices fluctuate. Advantages: realistic inventory valuation reflecting actual costs. In AX/D365, equivalent valuation methods are configured in Item Model Groups (InventModelGroup): Standard Cost = SAP Standard Price, Weighted Average = closest to SAP Moving Average.""}]"

The three documents that must match: 1) Purchase Order (EKKO/EKPO) - agreed quantity and price, 2) Goods Receipt (MKPF/MSEG) - actual quantity received, 3) Vendor Invoice (RBKP/RSEG) - vendor's billed quantity and price. The three documents: 1) Purchase Order (PurchTable/PurchLine) - ordered quantity and price, 2) Product Receipt (VendPackingSlipJour) - received quantity, 3) Vendor Invoice (VendInvoiceInfoTable) - billed amount. Matching policy is configured at Legal Entity or Vendor level: Two-way matching (PO vs Invoice), Three-way matching (PO + Product Receipt vs Invoice), or Charges matching (freight/surcharges). During invoice entry (VendInvoiceJour posting), AX checks quantity and price variances against tolerances. Invoices with matching exceptions are blocked and appear in the matching exceptions workbench for resolution. Successful matching required before invoice can be posted and paid.""}]"

Credit Memo: issued when you need to reduce what a customer owes you or what you owe a vendor. Customer Credit Memo (RE document type): created in SD with reference to original billing document, reverses revenue and reduces customer balance. Vendor Credit Memo: in FI with transaction FB65, reduces the vendor's open balance (you owe less). Debit Memo: issued to charge additional amounts. In AX/D365: Free Text Credit Notes for customers (CustFreeInvoice with negative amounts), Vendor Credit Notes (VendInvoiceJour with Credit Note type). The principle is identical - credit reduces balance, debit increases it.""}]"

Advantages: realistic inventory valuation reflecting actual costs. In AX/D365, equivalent valuation methods are configured in Item Model Groups (InventModelGroup): Standard Cost = SAP Standard Price, Weighted Average = closest to SAP Moving Average.""}]"

Payment blocks occur for several reasons: Invoice Verification block (R) - set automatically when 3-way matching fails (quantity or price variance beyond tolerance during MIRO); Manual block - set by finance/AP team (FB02 or MRBR); Vendor master block - vendor account itself is blocked (FK05). Standard Price (S): a fixed price set for the material that does not change with actual purchasing prices. All GR postings are made at this standard price. Price differences between actual PO price and standard price are posted to a Price Difference account. Used for: finished goods (FERT) and semi-finished goods (HALB) where production costs are planned. Advantages: stable inventory values, variance analysis highlighting inefficiencies. Moving Average Price (V): automatically recalculates after each goods receipt to reflect the actual average purchase price. Formula: (Current Stock Value + New GR Value) / (Current Stock Qty + New GR Qty). Used for: raw materials (ROH) and trading goods (HAWA) where market prices fluctuate. Advantages: realistic inventory valuation reflecting actual costs. In AX/D365, equivalent valuation methods are configured in Item Model Groups (InventModelGroup): Standard Cost = SAP Standard Price, Weighted Average = closest to SAP Moving Average.""}]"

In inter-plant stock transfers (within one company code): stock transfer order (STO) with movement type 641 (GI from sending plant), stock appears as 'Stock in Transfer' in MARD table (field UMLME) until goods receipt at receiving plant (movement type 101). In intercompany scenarios: billing document issued by selling company, goods in transit period before GR at buying company. Accounting treatment during transit: Goods in Transit account debited (asset account showing stock owned but not yet at destination). In AX/D365, goods in transit is managed through Transfer Orders (InventTransferTable) where ship status creates 'Shipped' inventory status visible in InventTrans with StatusIssue=Deducted at source and StatusReceipt=Purchased at destination before receipt posting.""}]"

The three documents that must match: 1) Purchase Order (EKKO/EKPO) - agreed quantity and price, 2) Goods Receipt (MKPF/MSEG) - actual quantity received, 3) Vendor Invoice (RBKP/RSEG) - vendor's billed quantity and price. This ensures you only pay for what was ordered AND received at the agreed price.""}]"

Disposal posts: Accumulated Depreciation Dr, Asset Account Cr, Gain/Loss on Disposal. All transactions stored in ANLP (depreciation) and ANLA/ANLZ (master data).""}]"

Purchase Requisition: internal document created by a department requesting materials or services (ME51N). No legal commitment, not sent to vendor, requires approval/release before converting to PO. Workflow: PR created by end user → approved by manager → Purchasing creates PO from PR (ME57/ME59) → PO sent to vendor → GR posted → Invoice verified. In AX/D365: Purchase Requisition (PurchReqTable) → Purchase Order (PurchTable) with the same approval workflow concept.""}]"

It is essential for maintaining the integrity between subledger and General Ledger without manual reconciliation. Importance: ensures subledger always equals GL, simplifies period-end reconciliation, provides audit trail. Advantages: realistic inventory valuation reflecting actual costs. In AX/D365, equivalent valuation methods are configured in Item Model Groups (InventModelGroup): Standard Cost = SAP Standard Price, Weighted Average = closest to SAP Moving Average.""}]"

The three documents that must match: 1) Purchase Order (EKKO/EKPO) - agreed quantity and price, 2) Goods Receipt (MKPF/MSEG) - actual quantity received, 3) Vendor Invoice (RBKP/RSEG) - vendor's billed quantity and price. This ensures you only pay for what was ordered AND received at the agreed price.""}]"

Standard Price (S): a fixed price set for the material that does not change with actual purchasing prices. All GR postings are made at this standard price. Price differences between actual PO price and standard price are posted to a Price Difference account. Used for: finished goods (FERT) and semi-finished goods (HALB) where production costs are planned. Advantages: stable inventory values, variance analysis highlighting inefficiencies. Moving Average Price (V): automatically recalculates after each goods receipt to reflect the actual average purchase price. Formula: (Current Stock Value + New GR Value) / (Current Stock Qty + New GR Qty). Used for: raw materials (ROH) and trading goods (HAWA) where market prices fluctuate. Advantages: realistic inventory valuation reflecting actual costs. In AX/D365, equivalent valuation methods are configured in Item Model Groups (InventModelGroup): Standard Cost = SAP Standard Price, Weighted Average = closest to SAP Moving Average.""}]"

The three documents that must match: 1) Purchase Order (EKKO/EKPO) - agreed quantity and price, 2) Goods Receipt (MKPF/MSEG) - actual quantity received, 3) Vendor Invoice (RBKP/RSEG) - vendor's billed quantity and price. During Invoice Verification (MIRO), SAP automatically compares: Invoice quantity vs GR quantity (quantity check), Invoice price vs PO price (price check). Tolerances are configured per company code. If invoice exceeds tolerance, it is automatically blocked (payment block R). Finance can review blocked invoices in MRBR. This ensures you only pay for what was ordered AND received at the agreed price.""}]"

Disposal posts: Accumulated Depreciation Dr, Asset Account Cr, Gain/Loss on Disposal. All transactions stored in ANLP (depreciation) and ANLA/ANLZ (master data).""}]"

Vendor Credit Memo: in FI with transaction FB65, reduces the vendor's open balance (you owe less). Debit Memo: issued to charge additional amounts. Customer Debit Memo (L2): additional charges to customer, increases customer balance. Vendor Debit Memo: you claim money back from vendor for overcharges. In AX/D365: Free Text Credit Notes for customers (CustFreeInvoice with negative amounts), Vendor Credit Notes (VendInvoiceJour with Credit Note type). The principle is identical - credit reduces balance, debit increases it.""}]"

It is essential for maintaining the integrity between subledger and General Ledger without manual reconciliation. Typical Reconciliation Accounts: 160000 (Accounts Payable), 140000 (Accounts Receivable), 170000 (Assets). Importance: ensures subledger always equals GL, simplifies period-end reconciliation, provides audit trail. In AX/D365, this concept is implemented through Posting Profiles (CustPostingProfile, VendPostingProfile) that map transaction types to specific Main Accounts.""}]"

Payment blocks occur for several reasons: Invoice Verification block (R) - set automatically when 3-way matching fails (quantity or price variance beyond tolerance during MIRO); Manual block - set by finance/AP team (FB02 or MRBR); Vendor master block - vendor account itself is blocked (FK05). The payment block indicator is stored in BSEG field ZLSPR (payment block key). To review blocked invoices: use MRBR (Release Blocked Invoices) for IV blocks, or FBL1N for all vendor open items filtered by payment block. Resolving IV blocks requires either approving the variance or requesting a credit memo from the vendor. In AX/D365, equivalent is the Invoice on-hold status or Approval workflow rejection blocking payment in VendInvoiceJour (ApprovalStatus field).""}]"

Standard Price (S): a fixed price set for the material that does not change with actual purchasing prices. All GR postings are made at this standard price. Price differences between actual PO price and standard price are posted to a Price Difference account. Used for: finished goods (FERT) and semi-finished goods (HALB) where production costs are planned. Advantages: stable inventory values, variance analysis highlighting inefficiencies. Moving Average Price (V): automatically recalculates after each goods receipt to reflect the actual average purchase price. Formula: (Current Stock Value + New GR Value) / (Current Stock Qty + New GR Qty). Used for: raw materials (ROH) and trading goods (HAWA) where market prices fluctuate. Advantages: realistic inventory valuation reflecting actual costs. In AX/D365, equivalent valuation methods are configured in Item Model Groups (InventModelGroup): Standard Cost = SAP Standard Price, Weighted Average = closest to SAP Moving Average.""}]"

Standard Price (S): a fixed price set for the material that does not change with actual purchasing prices. All GR postings are made at this standard price. Key difference: SAP BP was introduced in S/4HANA as an evolution, while AX/D365 was designed with the Global Address Book (party model) from the beginning. Both solve the same problem: one record for companies that are both customers and vendors.""}]"

An IDoc has a defined structure: Control Record (sender/receiver system, message type), Data Records (the actual business data organized in segments), and Status Records (tracking the processing status). IDoc types correspond to business messages: ORDERS05 (Purchase Order), INVOIC02 (Invoice), DEBMAS07 (Customer Master). IDocs are used for: EDI with trading partners, SAP-to-SAP integration, and legacy system interfaces. Transaction WE02 monitors IDocs. In AX/D365, equivalent integration is done through Data Entities and the Data Management Framework (DMF), or through the Electronic Reporting (ER) framework for formatted exchanges.""}]"

It is essential for maintaining the integrity between subledger and General Ledger without manual reconciliation. How it works: When you post a vendor invoice (in AP), SAP simultaneously updates the Vendor subledger account (for vendor balance tracking) AND the Reconciliation G/L Account (for GL balance). You cannot post directly to a Reconciliation Account - it is marked as 'Recon. Account for Acct Type' in G/L account master. Typical Reconciliation Accounts: 160000 (Accounts Payable), 140000 (Accounts Receivable), 170000 (Assets). Importance: ensures subledger always equals GL, simplifies period-end reconciliation, provides audit trail. In AX/D365, this concept is implemented through Posting Profiles (CustPostingProfile, VendPostingProfile) that map transaction types to specific Main Accounts.""}]"

Types: Customer Posting Profile (CustPostingProfile) - controls how customer invoices, payments, and write-offs post to GL; Vendor Posting Profile (VendPostingProfile) - same for vendor transactions; Inventory Posting (InventPosting) - maps inventory transactions to stock accounts; Fixed Asset Posting Profile (AssetPostingProfile) - maps asset transactions to asset/depreciation accounts. Standard Price (S): a fixed price set for the material that does not change with actual purchasing prices. All GR postings are made at this standard price. Price differences between actual PO price and standard price are posted to a Price Difference account. Used for: finished goods (FERT) and semi-finished goods (HALB) where production costs are planned. Advantages: stable inventory values, variance analysis highlighting inefficiencies. Moving Average Price (V): automatically recalculates after each goods receipt to reflect the actual average purchase price. Formula: (Current Stock Value + New GR Value) / (Current Stock Qty + New GR Qty). Used for: raw materials (ROH) and trading goods (HAWA) where market prices fluctuate. Advantages: realistic inventory valuation reflecting actual costs. In AX/D365, equivalent valuation methods are configured in Item Model Groups (InventModelGroup): Standard Cost = SAP Standard Price, Weighted Average = closest to SAP Moving Average.""}]"
